quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to show your intentions.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane. Do not use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers in which situation?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians crossing on a sidewalk.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you with high beams on. Where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an approaching vehicle is using high beams and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and allows you to stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: Can you drive on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal?

options.text: No, under no circumstances.
Yes, if the property owner gives permission.
Yes, if you are running late.
Yes, if a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a police officer directs you to do so.
questions.explanation: Driving on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal is illegal unless a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be driving slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often drive slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching a large truck from behind. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move when a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: A solid yellow line and a broken yellow line are in the center of the road. The broken line is next to your lane. When may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
When traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop. Release the gas to slow down, then brake gently. This activates your brake lights and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
Lane ends or road narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, what is important to remember?

options.text: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Trucks pass faster on downhill slopes than smaller vehicles.
Trucks turn in a smaller space than smaller vehicles.
Trucks pass faster on uphill slopes than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and heavier, so they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After turning, where should your car be?

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the left lane, which is closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: An officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign stopping you from doing so.

questions.question: You should check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from. This keeps your turn safe and smooth.

questions.question: A sign of an aggressive driver is that they:

options.text: Do not yield the right-of-way properly.
Keep a three-second distance from other cars.
Never change lanes.
Drive with a broken headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not yield the right-of-way properly.
questions.explanation: Aggressive drivers are dangerous. They make unsafe moves like changing lanes suddenly, following too close, and not yielding the right-of-way. Do not confront an aggressive driver.

questions.question: What color are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give information about where to go are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it since all cars are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with it.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where everything is and how to use it before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where everything is and how to use it before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, take time to find and understand the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You stay calm and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stay calm and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it hard to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or focus better.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Move in the direction the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after letting oncoming cars and pedestrians pass.
Go ahead because you have the right-of-way and others will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Cancels out the alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving car?

options.text: Only the driver
Only adult passengers
Only child passengers
Everyone in the car

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car
questions.explanation: By law, the driver and all passengers must wear seat belts. It is against the law for the driver, front seat passengers, or anyone under 18 to not wear a seat belt. The driver is responsible for making sure all passengers under 18 buckle up. Unbelted back seat passengers 18 and older may get a ticket if the car is stopped for another reason.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, you should signal first, check both mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. You must treat it the same way as a stop sign.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop if you can, unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Look both ways before going through the intersection.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Be extra careful and watch for children and pedestrians when you see this sign.

questions.question: How must a driver treat pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always let them cross first, even if they are breaking the rules.
Only yield when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let them cross first, even if they are breaking the rules.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, regardless of who is at fault. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Proceed slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before you go.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look both ways, then go if traffic is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a "Yield" sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles cross first. Only stop if necessary.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Make your engine use more oil.
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner.
Make you sleepy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. A leak can release dangerous fumes that make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: Which rule applies to drivers with a probationary license?

options.text: They can use a hand-held cell phone while driving.
They must wear a seat belt, but their passengers do not have to.
They cannot use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
They can drive without a seat belt if they choose to.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Probationary license drivers must follow special rules. They cannot use any cell phone, hand-held or hands-free. They must wear a seat belt at all times while driving.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road as far as possible before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes to make your turn.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause hearing loss.
It can cause pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It can cause poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gas and prevents fumes from entering the passenger area. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the vehicle. Fix leaks right away to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. All drivers must stop and take turns. Proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: What helps drivers avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to the vehicle for better grip.
Leave highways as fast as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. Increasing your following distance is the most important way to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge smoothly.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, which side should a pedestrian walk on?

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side traffic is moving.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces traffic coming toward them.
